summary: Larch Mountain lookout, Clark County, WA: 40-foot tower built 1952, weather station after 1969, gone by 1974; a federal survey record labels a radar tower on the mountain.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden tower with L-4 cab (14x14 ft)
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed (or removed) in 1974. A federal survey record labels a point on the mountain LARCH MTN RADAR TOWER but gives no station description

staffing.status: Charles Briggs was observing from the lookout in November 1952; opening delayed by snow in May 1955; discontinued for fire duty in August 1969 and kept as a weather station

access.note: Mountain lies within Yacolt Burn State Forest. Willhite describes walking a road from the Larch Mountain Trailhead; a gate just below the trailhead is closed in winter

visit.trail_note: No lookout tower remains to climb. Willhite describes walking up the road from the Larch Mountain Trailhead Parking Area

events.note: 40-foot timber or wooden tower with 14x14 L-4 cab, built by the state forestry division
Charles Briggs relayed reports from the lookout in November 1952 until the Yacolt burn fire forced him to leave
Yacolt burn fire reached the mountain's east slope in November 1952
Opening of the station delayed by snow drifts in spring 1955; usual opening April 15
Discontinued as a fire lookout in August 1969 when air patrols took over detection; kept as a weather station
Destroyed in 1974 per the Fire Lookout website and Willhite; the register says removed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register June 24, 2012

evidence.supports: 40-ft wooden tower with L-4 cab built 1952; register says removed 1974
evidence.quote: This 40' wooden tower with L-4 cab, built in 1952, was removed in 1974.

evidence.supports: 40-ft wooden tower with L-4 cab built 1952; destroyed 1974
evidence.quote: This 40' wooden tower with L-4 cab, built in 1952, was destroyed in 1974.

evidence.supports: administered by Washington Division of Forestry/DNR
1952 40-foot timber tower with 14x14 cab erected (Annual Report, Forestry Division)
evidence.quote: 1952: A 40-foot timber tower with a 14'x14' cab was erected.

evidence.supports: only known lookout built 1952; DNR built 40-ft timber tower with 14x14 L-4 cab
evidence.quote: The only known lookout built was in 1952 when the DNR built a 40 foot timber tower with a 14x14 foot L-4 cab on top.

evidence.supports: November 1952 Yacolt burn fire; Charles Briggs relayed reports by radio until forced to leave
evidence.quote: Most reports about the blaze came by radio from Charles Briggs, from the state forestry lookout atop Washington's Larch mountain, but he was forced to leave the lookout late Saturday when the fire entered Clark county and began to climb the east slope of the mountain.

evidence.supports: snow drifts kept crews from opening the station in 1955
evidence.quote: He said drifts of snow seven feet deep are keeping his crews from getting the station open.

evidence.supports: usual opening of the station April 15
evidence.quote: Usual opening of Larch mountain is April 15.

evidence.supports: 1969 discontinued as one of five Battle Ground district lookouts; air patrol took over detection
evidence.quote: Larch Mountain lookout is one of five lookouts on the Battle Ground district to be discontinued as the result of detection duties being taken over by air patrol.

evidence.supports: station maintained as weather station to report east winds in the Columbia Gorge
evidence.quote: But, this particular station was maintained as a weather station because it is was located to give the best reports of the rising east winds through the Columbia Gorge.
In 1974, the Larch Mountain lookout tower was destroyed.

evidence.supports: NGS survey record designation LARCH MTN RADAR TOWER, Clark County
NGS record has no station description (as quoted on the weebly page)
mountain lies within Yacolt Burn State Forest, laced with gravel roads
evidence.quote: It is laced by a network of gravel roads as part of the Yacolt Burn State Forest.

evidence.supports: walkable road from the Larch Mountain Trailhead Parking Area
evidence.quote: A good road can be walked from the Larch Mountain Trailhead Parking Area

evidence.supports: gate closed in winter just below the trailhead
evidence.quote: In winter, a gate will be closed just a short distance below the trailhead on the L-1500 road.

evidence.supports: a more famous Larch Mountain lookout is on the Oregon side of the Columbia Gorge
evidence.quote: Note that there is a more famous Larch Mountain Lookout on the Oregon side of the Columbia Gorge.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1974; the Fire Lookout website and Willhite say destroyed. All agree on 1974.

notes_for_editor: Build, 1969 weather-station change and 1974 end are consistent across sources; the register says removed and two sources say destroyed. The NGS point for RD2248 (45 43 01.10077 N, 122 17 44.47742 W) sits at the brief's coordinates, but the record has no station description, so whether a radar tower stands today is unverified. Access 'public' is inferred from state-forest land and a trailhead; check the land manager's rules before stating more. Willhite's 2022 drone photo captions describe no structure, so they are not cited. Oregon's Larch Mountain lookout is a different site and is mentioned only to prevent confusion.
